approach: Detonation physics. One pure model (CombatLights.hpp/.cpp, "Detonation") replaces the classic blast size (hit x 0.003, clamped 0.25..1), which measured penetration rather than explosive. Charge W = indirectHit x indirectHitRange / 480 kg TNT, which is the engine's own crater energy, calibrated so Shell120 comes out at 2.5 kg. A round is a shaped charge when hit > that energy. Lengths and times scale with s = W^(1/3) (Hopkinson-Cranz): fireball radius 1.6 s m, flash e-folding time 0.03 s x s, afterburn 0.12 s x s (a third of that for shaped charges). Gas temperature is 3200 K falling to a 2000 K afterburn, then to 900 K soot. Fireball puffs are born at the gas temperature of their moment, half of them during the flash, and are drawn in the frame they are born (before this, new puffs only appeared 1 to 2 frames late and already cooled). Light is 350 x W^(2/3) x Wien(T against the peak) in the black-body colour. The dust and soot column is 6 m x s high and lasts 12 s x s, drifts with the wind and throws earth. Fuel burns as a deflagration from the CCPS fireball formulas (diameter 5.8 M^(1/3) m, duration 0.45 M^(1/3) s) at a 1900 K sooty flame, with black soot and a wreck that keeps burning. It now fires for cars as well, while the damage and sound keep their original gate. Lighting fixes: a burst's light on the ground fades out within at most 10 m at lower gain (0.12; fuel 0.04), the burst's air scatter is half its ball, a fireball puff is not lit by its own blast, blast light keeps its hue on smoke, and the fireball glow follows the bursts' night scale.

approach: A per-munition look table in a new engine module, engine/Poseidon/Graphics/Rendering/Effects/BlastLook.hpp/.cpp. It sorts every explosion into one of 8 classes using config data only: CfgAmmo simulation, and a charge of 0.002 kg x indirectHit x indirectHitRange. The classes are grenade, HE shell, HEAT, rocket warhead, satchel, mine, bomb and fuel tank. The engine has no ammo cook-off, so there is no row for it. Each row sets the flash (length of the combat-light envelope, its tint and power), the fireball (CfgCloudlets Explosion puffs: emit time, life, birth temperature and cooling rate, size, spread, rise), the smoke column, dust skirt and haze (crater smoke 1/2/3: colour, alpha, emit time, life, size, rise), and the number of thrown earth clods. Sizes and times scale with the cube root of the charge. The table drives the existing systems and draws nothing new. Shots.cpp (all 7 explosion sites) and Collisions.cpp (the crater) classify from the AmmoType. The fuel-explosion path uses the fuel-tank row. CombatLights gets a time scale per burst (each record has a span and the envelope is read at age / span) and honours a tint on Explosion lights. Fireball puffs are born above the ground and the ball is lifted, so it no longer shows a flat cut. The smoke column only starts once the fireball has cooled; before, it hid the glow from the second frame on.

approach:
High explosive against fuel, fixed in the emitters. I took the munition data from the config dump and the code: CfgAmmo, CfgCloudlets Explosion and CraterSmoke1-3, Shots.cpp, Collisions.cpp, Dammage.cpp and Smokes.cpp. Every number now lives in one header-only file, BlastLook.hpp.
(1) Explosion size now comes from the charge (cube root of indirectHit x range against Shell120) instead of the direct hit. Before, a HEAT round drew the largest fireball of all.
(2) The HE flash: puffs are born at 3000 K and cool to 1500 K in 0.1 s times the linear scale. They reach full size by their first drawn frame (before, they grew from size 0 and were first drawn a step after birth, so the white-hot birth was never seen). They are born on the upper half of the ball only, so the ground no longer cuts the bottom flat. The soot that follows spreads slowly and hangs for 2.3 s instead of 0.4 s. The burst light now starts one step later, together with the first drawn puffs.
(3) The crater's three smoke sources are replaced by code-set looks: thrown dark earth, a grey-brown column that decelerates and hangs, and a low dust skirt. They last about 5 to 17 s, scaled by crater size, in fixed dark colours (the config's colour table drifted them toward white).
(4) Fuel: the fireball now burns on every vehicle explosion, not only past the hit > 50 damage gate, which a Jeep never passes. The damage gate itself is unchanged. The fireball puffs are born at 2150 K and cool 380 K/s, are emitted for about 0.9 s, are 5x larger, roll out slowly, and black soot goes up with them. The wreck then burns about 45 s plus a 30 s fade. The fireball's light is carried on the embers' Fire light, and the white burst light is halved.

approach: Rendering of fire and flash. (1) Fireball puffs now carry an HDR glow: Object::DrawDecal keeps a fireball's glow above white as a gain (new Engine::SetDecalGlowGain). The GL33 backend passes it in the decal's second texture coordinate with a tag (kDecalGlowGainTag), and the pre-lit shader multiplies the glow by it only when the tag is present, so the hot core is stored above white, the camera curve whitens it and the bloom picks it up. (2) Each puff glows by its own temperature: FireballPuff emission 8 -> 137 and cap 2 -> 9 (white at 2500 K, yellow-orange at 2000 K, orange at 1600 K, soot from 1300 K). Cooling is set per munition at the source: cased charges cool at 5000/cbrt(size) K/s, while the fuel tank burns as a deflagration (born at 1950 K, cooling 550 K/s, longer-lived, rising, 4x size, and a Fire-kind light with an envelope instead of a detonation flash). (3) PrimeFireballBirth makes a new fireball puff visible at 0.7 of its size on the frame it is born. Before this, new puffs were drawn transparent at size 0, so the flash frame had no fireball. (4) Fireball puffs are lifted so that their centre sits at least 0.7 of their radius above the ground, which removes the flat cut-off bottom. (5) The detonation flash lasts tens of ms and scales with the cube root of the charge (tau 0.025 s, glow 0.07 s), with no 0.15 s hold under the camera. The burst's light on the ground is scaled down 0.3x so its centre no longer clips into a flat white disc. One harness finding: each captured frame is about 0.1 s of simulation, not 1/30 s (triScreenshot at present lets several fixed steps run), so the clips play about 3x too fast.

approach: Time and lifetimes. First I checked the clock: every explosion stage already runs on the simulation step. Cloudlets use deltaT in SimulateCloudlets, Explosion/Crater/fuel SmokeSource use SimulateRest with deltaT under 1/15 s, and combat lights use Tick(deltaT). So the blink was not a clock bug. The stages had the wrong lengths, and one stage was never run. Changes: (1) Shell explosions are sized by the cube root of the charge (indirectHit x indirectHitRange) instead of the direct hit. HEAT was the biggest burst; it is now 0.38 against HE's 0.6. (2) Fireball puffs cool past glowing within a flash of 0.1 x size s: HE 60 ms, HEAT 38 ms, grenade 28 ms. The old -4000 K/s kept them glowing 0.2 s. (3) The Explosion combat light hold and decays scale by min(size,1), so the light lasts as long as the flash. (4) The crater smoke column lingers. Puffs hold 9xL s and fade over 9xL s, the rise decays to a hang at about 18 m, the dark cloud no longer whitens with age, and lingering puffs keep spreading and relax to the landscape wind (new Cloudlet::SetLinger). (5) CraterDustBig (a thrown-earth dust curtain that falls back within about 2 s) now runs for big bursts; before, it was loaded but never run. (6) Any vehicle fuel now burns as a deflagration. The blast damage stays gated at hit>50, so gameplay is unchanged. The fireball uses bigger puffs born at 2150 K and cooling at -420 K/s (about 0.83 s of glow each), rising with buoyancy, plus black soot that lives 8 s and a Fire-kind combat light for the burn.

approach: Art direction within physics. Rules: a cased charge is a one-frame white-hot dome flash sitting on the ground, then a short orange afterburn, then no glow, and never a Hollywood fireball. Size and glow time scale with the cube root of the charge, read from the ammo's blast (indirectHit x indirectHitRange, 120 mm HE = 1200 as reference). HE scales to 1, HEAT to 0.63 (shaped charge: narrower and taller), grenade to 0.47. What lingers is earth: thrown clods and a dark grey-brown column that drifts for many seconds. Fuel deflagrates as a big, slow, orange (never white) rolling ball under black soot, sized by the fuel fireball rules D = 5.8 M^(1/3) and t = 0.45 M^(1/3). Light sits inside the fireball, lasts as long as the fire and fades out as a pool with no rim. Root causes found and proven with a temporary DrawDecal log (now removed): (1) The classic fireball puffs stepped through 47 streamed cl_fired texture frames in 0.5 s, so after the first frame the puffs mostly had no texture loaded and were not drawn. That was the one-frame fire. (2) New puffs stayed invisible for two frames while the light already lit the ground. (3) A destroyed Jeep never had a fuel explosion, because GetExplosives counts only ammo for a plain Transport. (4) The burst's surface window at 3 core radii plus the 0.3 gain drew a flat bright disc. (5) The big crater's dust jet was never simulated, and its smoke lived only 2 to 3 s.
owner_line: Each munition now has its own explosion. The 120 mm HE gives a one-frame white-hot dome on the ground, an orange flicker, then thrown earth and a dark brown column that drifts for over 10 s. The grenade is a small flash and a small brown puff. The HEAT round is a narrower yellow flash with a thin column. A destroyed Jeep's fuel goes up as a 14 m orange ball that rolls into black soot over about half a second, lights the area for about a second, and leaves the wreck smoking for 40 s.

per_munition:
120 mm HE (scale 1, fireball radius 2.4 m): frame 1 is a white-hot dome about 5 m across sitting on the ground, with a soft lit pool under it. Frame 2 is an orange afterburn ball fading into brown dust. From frame 3: dark clods and 20 to 30 dust puffs thrown up to about 10 m that fall back, and a dark grey-brown column about 15 m tall within 1 s, about 20 m wide by 2 s, drifting. Puffs live about 12 s plus about 5 s of fade (before: gone by about 3 s).
Hand grenade (scale 0.47): 1 frame of a small yellow-white flash (about 2.4 m) with a soft ground glow, 1 frame of a small orange ball (about 3 m), then a brown puff a few metres across lingering about 6 s.
120 mm HEAT (scale 0.63, shaped): 1 frame of a narrow, taller yellow-white flash, 1 pale remnant frame, then a narrow dark column lingering about 9 s.
Jeep fuel (none before): an orange ball growing to about 14 m within 0.2 s and rolling up under black soot. It stays orange for about 0.4 s and is black soot by about 0.6 s. Its Fire-kind light lasts 1.1 s, then the wreck smokes for 40 s. At night the ball is bright orange and lights the plain warm, but its soot turns pale grey under its own light.
Night HE: a white dome flash for 1 frame lighting ground and men, an orange frame, then dim earth-coloured dust (darker than the round 5 grey).
weak_points:
1. Smoke now lingers, so it drifts into later clips of the shared test. The staged burning Ural also gets its own fuel ball and smokes heavily for 40 s, so the backgrounds differ from the before clips.
2. The HE flash is a single frame and the afterburn one to two frames: a sharp pop by design, but whether the flash lands on a captured frame depends on timing.
3. One crater smoke puff sometimes shoots up much faster than the rest (a dark ball reaching about 20 m in HE frames 13 to 18). I did not find its source.
4. At night the fuel ball's soot is lit pale grey by its own fire light, so the thick black soot only holds at dusk. kFuelBallLight is the knob; I already lowered it from 9 to 5.
5. All burst puffs use the first frame of cl_basic, so close up the puffs share one shape.
6. From eye height the ground pool still reads as a soft ellipse for 1 to 2 frames. It has no rim and stays under the fire.
7. Not checked: the rocket (LAW, RPG) path. Missiles also get SetBlast and the new burst. I did not look into the LAW probe's black lower-half frame.
8. Every destroyed vehicle with 2 l of fuel or more now gets a fuel ball, aircraft and ships included (capped at 16 m and 2 s). Not shot.
9. The classic lighting path was not shot.
10. No frame-time numbers: the munition tests read no timers. tri wall time was 156 s against 220 s before, with a different machine load. Particle counts: about 70 puffs at peak per HE burst for 0.3 s, then about 36 crater smoke puffs alive for about 15 s instead of about 3 s, so a barrage keeps roughly 5 times as many smoke puffs alive.
